solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Husband straying? He might catch this!

parts.note: erring means wandering from the right path, straying

explanation.surface: A wife suspects her husband is playing away, and warns that he might catch something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'catch' suggests a disease picked up by a philandering husband; in the definition 'He' is a fisherman landing a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman at sea might land this silvery shoal fish in his nets.

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another: the letter for Henry takes the place of the letter for large in the word leave

parts.note: L is the usual abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
H is the henry, the SI unit of inductance

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave out a man called Henry in favour of a big American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American, but it is the verb: to pull hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to pull with a strong sudden effort, which is to haul or lug something.

clue.text: Respond to provocation, as creature of the deep may do?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for reacting angrily to a taunt

definitions.text: as creature of the deep may do?
definitions.meaning: literally, a fish swims up to take the angler's lure

explanation.surface: Someone reacting to a goad is compared to a fish going for a hook.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for reacting to a taunt comes from a fish surfacing to snap at a lure.

definitions.meaning: children or offspring, in the legal sense of descendants
a matter in dispute or a difficulty

explanation.surface: A weary parent remarks that children can be trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person's offspring and a point of contention or difficulty.

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with or alter it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to look into a medic working in the West African country of Togo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' reads as a physician but is a verb signalling the letters of IN TOGO are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine a matter closely is a phrasal-verb synonym for investigating it.

indicators.note: the evening meal is spelt with a doubled letter p; allowing just one of them means dropping the other

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A diner praises a lovely meal but grumbles that it cost only a penny, or had a single p.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is an informal adjective for excellent or wonderful.

indicators.note: the French article is placed after the word for kick-off

parts.note: the kick-off is the start of a football match
le is the French masculine for 'the'

explanation.surface: The French team are caught unawares straight after a match begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to give them a sudden shock or surprise.

clue.text: Prepare clergyman for the highest office?

definitions.note: names the post by its holder; the question mark admits the stretch from person to office

parts.note: to prime is to make ready, as with a pump or a canvas
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A clergyman is being groomed for a top job, perhaps a bishopric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clergyman' suggests church office, but the answer is the head of a government, here the British one.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of government holds the most senior political post in Britain, so the title stands for that office.

indicators.note: the words Overran Cherokees contain the answer within them, as if holding it

explanation.surface: A Western scene: Cherokees overrun a settlement and take a cowboy prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher runs a cattle ranch, and in loose usage a cowboy is anyone who herds cattle.

clue.text: Killing of one donkey after another by island people

indicators.note: one donkey followed by another gives the same word twice in a row

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Island people slaughter donkeys one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassination is the murder of a prominent person, a particular kind of killing.

clue.text: Beg Parisian in hospital to abandon threat

parts.note: en is French for 'in', as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: the letter for hospital deserts the word threat, so it is removed

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A Frenchman in hospital pleads for a menace to be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to ask earnestly, to implore or plead.

clue.text: Ethel regularly chewed the things in her mouth

indicators.note: taking every other letter of Ethel, at regular intervals
chewing mangles something, so the letters of 'the' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ethel routinely munched on the items she had in her mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd and 4th letters of Ethel, TE; 'chewed' rearranges THE to ETH.
explanation.definitionFit: The chewing implements in anyone's mouth are the dentition, the set of biting structures.

clue.text: Punt unsteadily, drinking old whiskey in residential area

indicators.note: one thing taking in another, as a drinker takes in liquor
a wobbly punt suggests its letters are jumbled

parts.note: W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy on old whiskey punts wobbily through a suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsteadily' rearranges PUNT to UPTN; 'drinking' puts O and W inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiefly in American use, the upper or outlying part of a city where people live, away from the business district.

indicators.note: out signals the letters are disordered or wrong, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nobody put the rats outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nobody' reads as 'no one' but is the noun: an unimportant person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person of no standing; an upstart is a presumptuous newcomer of low rank.

clue.text: One who observes criminal a wretch

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An observer accuses a wretch of being a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher is an onlooker or observer.

indicators.note: the Spanish title goes round the letter for India, as a tourist goes round a country

parts.note: señor is Spanish for a gentleman or Mr
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An elderly Spaniard is on a tour of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior describes someone of greater age or longer standing.

indicators.note: in a down clue, one word sits above the other, as if looking down on it

parts.note: Doctor Who is the BBC's time-travelling TV hero
ops are surgical operations or procedures

explanation.surface: A doctor misses something in surgery, and someone exclaims in dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' suggests a doctor's negligence; in a down light it means sitting above. Doctor Who is the long-running BBC science-fiction hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of mild dismay at a mistake or mishap.

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the word, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: sent means dispatched, sent off

explanation.surface: A journalist's scent has been posted off somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Scent is a fragrance worn on the skin, the same as a perfume.

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so the letters are blown into a new order

explanation.surface: Some cloth is left in ashes after a blast.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessian is a coarse woven cloth of jute or hemp, used for sacks.

indicators.note: the family word is put inside the street word

parts.note: kin are family, relatives

explanation.surface: A broke family is cast out onto the street.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for broke, having no money at all.

clue.text: Ideal position of hotel in French resort

indicators.note: the letter for hotel goes inside the resort name

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel in Nice is perfectly placed.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a role or place exactly suited to someone, their perfect spot.

clue.text: Thracian coins misrepresented as belonging to another time

indicators.note: letters represented wrongly are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Ancient Thracian coins are wrongly dated by a collector.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anachronistic is out of its proper period, set in the wrong era.

clue.text: Rubbish written by Her Majesty — or King Edward

indicators.note: the royal initials are written beside, after, the word for rubbish

parts.note: tat is cheap tasteless junk
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: Junk written by the Queen, or by a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Edward' looks royal, but it is a British potato variety; 'tater' is slang for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: King Edward is a popular British variety of potato, and a tater is a colloquial spud.

parts.note: a set is a group of people, a crowd or gang
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: A gang is let out with no charges laid.
explanation.definitionFit: To set free is to liberate, the same as releasing someone.
